\label{proposition-lefschetz-equivalence}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module
and let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{L})$. Let $Y = Z(s)$
be the zero scheme of $s$ and denote $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_X$
the corresponding sheaf of ideals.
Let $\mathcal{V}$ be the set of open subschemes of $X$ containing $Y$
ordered by reverse inclusion.
Assume that for all $x \in X \setminus Y$ we have
$$
\text{depth}(\mathcal{O}_{X, x}) + \dim(\overline{\{x\}}) > 2
$$
Then the completion functor
$$
\colim_\mathcal{V}
\textit{Coh}(\mathcal{O}_V)
\longrightarrow
\textit{Coh}(X, \mathcal{I})
$$
is an equivalence on the full subcategories of finite locally free objects.
statement:
For a Noetherian local ring $(A,\mathfrak m)$, the punctured spectrum is $\operatorname{Spec}(A)\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$. The Picard group $\operatorname{Pic}(U)$ classifies invertible $\mathcal O_U$-modules. For a Noetherian scheme $X$ and a sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I$, let $\textit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ denote compatible formal coherent systems on the infinitesimal thickenings defined by $\mathcal I^n$. Completion of a coherent sheaf is its system of reductions to these thickenings. A colimit over opens containing a closed locus is taken via restrictions to smaller opens.
